rationale: SW-D21 (#938, swift lane, full extent 554 files of swift-nio): a switch-case PATTERN with an associated value does not reduce in the pinned grammar — `case .websocket(let channel):` recovers as a call_expression whose callee navigation STARTS AT THE `case` KEYWORD (`simple_identifier "case"` + navigation_suffix + a call_suffix holding `let` and an ERROR). The pre-fix code took the leaf and published `calls -> websocket` / `calls -> notUpgraded`: the ONLY analyzer edges on the full-extent draw with no truth counterpart (3 rows over Client.swift/Server.swift, 1 red draw). The fix reads the reserved keyword off the token (never source text) and returns silently. The positive half pins that the fix is not a blanket suppression: the real call in `handle` (`consume(channel)`) and the genuinely different site sharing the leaf name (`UpgradeResult.websocket(1)` -> enum construction) both still have to be emitted.

expectRelationships.note: the real call inside the recovered case body — the keyword gate must not silence genuine calls in the same switch
`UpgradeResult.websocket(1)` — the enum construction whose leaf name the fabricated edges borrowed

forbidRelationships.comment: #938: the case PATTERN must never be published as a call
#938: neither pattern spelling may fabricate a call
#938: a pattern is not construction either — `case` is a reserved keyword, not a type name
